Pour faire bondir les recettes publiques, son ministère a impulsé la réforme de la facture dite « normalisée », un dispositif électronique qui institue une facture unique et informatisée, connectée à un serveur public. Il est censé permettre à l’État de connaître exactement le niveau de TVA collectée par les entreprises. stories.title: Sahara occidental: Washington veut réformer la Minurso, le Front Polisario menace de quitter les discussions
stories.summary: Sahara occidental: Washington veut réformer la Minurso, le Front Polisario menace de quitter les discussions La tension monte encore d'un cran à moins de dix jours du vote au siège de l'ONU de la prolongation ou non du mandat de la Minurso, la mission des Nations unies pour l'organisation d'un référendum au Sahara occidental. Un avant-projet présenté ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026 par les États-Unis au Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU redéfinit les contours de la mission onusienne. Washington préconise la prolongation du mandat de la Minurso, mais son rôle serait profondément modifié, ce qui a fait réagir très vite le Front Polisario, le groupe indépendantiste sahraoui, qui s’est senti visé. Publié le : 23/10/2026 - 12:24 4 min Temps de lecture Un véhicule de la mission de l'ONU au Sahara occidental (Minurso), le 13 mai 2013, à Laâyoune. © AFP Par : Sophiane Amazian Publicité Lire la suite Dans un document de trois pages consulté par RFI, les États-Unis , en tant que « porte-plume » (pays chargé de rédiger le premier projet de résolution, NDLR) , présentent dans leur première version de projet de résolution 14 mesures pour réformer la Minurso. Son nom d'abord : la Minurso deviendrait la Minuso, sans le « R », donc, de « référendum ».

stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, This is the first case of Ebola in Nigeria in more than a decade By Simi Jolaoso ,Â Africa correspondent ,Â Makuochi Okafor ,Â BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Lagos Â and Â Wycliffe Muia Published 23 October 2026, 05:54 BST Updated 1 hour ago Switzerland's foreign ministry has confirmed that the woman who has tested positive for Ebola in Nigeria is the wife of a Swiss diplomat. Camanor of the National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL) said the government, through the Ministry of Health and NPHIL, is closely monitoring the regional situation and taking precautionary measures to protect the population. stories.title: Mali: Army, Russia's 'Africa Corps' Commit New Abuses
stories.summary: Mali: Army, Russia's 'Africa Corps' Commit New Abuses Adrien Lefevre / Sahel Press Agency A military pickup carrying armed fighters drives past the iconic painted boulder marking the entrance to Kidal, a remote desert town in northern Mali long at the heart of the country's decade-long conflict between government forces, Tuareg movements, and armed groups operating across the Sahara. 22 October 2026 Human Rights Watch (Washington, DC) Nairobi — Unlawful Drone Strike, Torture of Civilians in Mopti Region Mali's armed forces and the allied Russia -controlled Africa Corps have committed new atrocities against civilians in central Mali during renewed fighting, Human Rights Watch said today. On September 16, 2026, an apparent military drone strike in Guélédié village, Mopti region, killed eight civilians and injured at least six others. Between May and August, Malian and Africa Corps forces held numerous detainees inhumanely in a metal container at an army base in Sévaré town, Mopti region, where many were tortured, including with severe beatings, electric shock, and waterboarding. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn "Civilians are bearing the brunt of the Mali junta's failure to rein in its abusive forces and allies," said Ilaria Allegrozzi , senior Sahel researcher at Human Rights Watch. "Recent atrocities implicate the Malian army as well as Russia-controlled Africa Corps, for which Russian officials should also be held accountable." The Malian army's offensive followed coordinated attacks across Mali by the Al Qaeda-linked Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, JNIM) and the Azawad Liberation Front (Front de Libération de l'Azawad, FLA) in late April. Malian forces and the allied Africa Corps killed civilians, including many children , and destroyed civilian property and health facilities in airstrikes and other attacks.

stories.title: Uganda: Ensure Justice for Killing of Rwandan Dissident
stories.summary: Uganda: Ensure Justice for Killing of Rwandan Dissident 22 October 2026 Human Rights Watch (Washington, DC) Nairobi — Authorities Worldwide Should Protect Rwandans Fleeing Persecution Ugandan authorities' obligation to conduct an effective investigation into the brutal killing of a Rwandan dissident requires examining all evidence that points to a possible politically motivated killing, Human Rights Watch said today. Ugandan authorities should ensure a prompt, impartial, credible investigation that leads to accountability. Robert Kabera, a singer, former Rwanda Defence Force member, and outspoken critic of the Rwandan government, was found on October 17, 2026, in Luwala village near Kampala, where he was constructing a house. He had fled Rwanda in November 2020 and claimed asylum on political persecution grounds. He had reported to Human Rights Watch multiple times that he had been threatened and attacked in Uganda.

stories.title: Africa: How K-Dramas Use Africa As a Backdrop to Boost South Korea's Image
stories.summary: Africa: How K-Dramas Use Africa As a Backdrop to Boost South Korea's Image 22 October 2026 The Conversation Africa (Johannesburg) analysis By Osarugue Otebele The success of South Korean popular music or K-pop continues to power the Hallyu Wave , a term that describes the global obsession with the country's pop culture production. But before K-pop came the spread of K-drama, TV series from the country, starting in the late 1990s. By 2024 the melodrama Queen of Tears ranked as the most watched Korean series on Netflix, becoming the 14th most watched show of all time on the streaming service. It followed on the success of many other hits like Crash Landing on You and Marry My Husband . K-drama has led to the development of another trend: Africa repeatedly appears as a homogeneous place full of savage danger or childish immaturity, and in need of a Korean saviour.

stories.title: Africa: Africa CDC Chief Warns 'No Country Is Safe' As Ebola Reaches Nigeria
stories.summary: Africa CDC Chief Warns 'No Country Is Safe' As Ebola Reaches Nigeria Grainne Harrington/WHO A patient is carried to an Ebola treatment centre in the DR Congo. 22 October 2026 Radio France Internationale By RFI The latest Ebola outbreak has killed nearly 4,700 people and is still spreading, with Nigeria recording its first case in more than a decade. The epidemic is not yet under control and tighter surveillance is needed, Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, told RFI. The Nigerian patient is a woman who returned to the capital, Abuja , from Uganda on 3 October. Kaseya said she had stayed in Kampala , the Ugandan capital, and had never visited the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). If his account is correct, it would point to transmission in Uganda, which the Ugandan authorities deny.

stories.summary: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola Responders Under Pressure As Outbreak Expands 22 October 2026 UN News Service As the deadly Ebola disease outbreak reached an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), investigators pursued all leads on Thursday to assess the risk of the disease spreading in Nigeria. Authorities in Abuja confirmed their first case of infection in an individual arriving from Uganda, which borders the worst-hit provinces in DRC. " The source of exposure is still not known and the travel history of the patient is being pieced together now in terms of her movement from Uganda up to Nigeria," said Dr Patrick Otim, from the UN World Health Organization ( WHO )'s Emergency Response programme, in an online update. " This is rapidly evolving. As we get more information, we'll try to determine where she was exposed . And then it's at that point where we can say whether there is any transmission happening." stories.title: Africa: 'Connect the Dots' Between Street Protests and Global Turmoil, Urges Guterres
stories.summary: Africa: 'Connect the Dots' Between Street Protests and Global Turmoil, Urges Guterres Tsoanelo Sefoloko/GroundUp One of several cars set alight in Durban city centre during a march by hundreds of anti-immigrant protesters. 22 October 2026 UN News Service The international community must combat inequality and stop wars from expanding to ensure a safer world for all, the UN Secretary-General said on Thursday. Speaking to reporters in New York ahead of a visit to Egypt, António Guterres addressed growing public discontent in Europe and beyond, as people have taken to the streets to express frustration over the rising cost of living. "Everywhere, pressures are building over the price of food, fuel and other basics," he said . " Interest rates are up - for people and countries. And for young people, the promise of a better future is slipping further out of reach." No fire without smoke Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines While Mr. Guterres clearly denounced the violence and destruction seen during days of protests in France, Italy and elsewhere - stressing that those responsible for criminal activities must be held accountable - he said legitimate grievances of the protestors cannot be overlooked. " We must connect the dots and better understand how deeply linked those very real and peacefully expressed grievances are to the wider turmoil in our world ," he told journalists. He said that today, conflicts are not only intensifying but expanding, which he likened to the El Niño climate phenomenon that occurs in one region but disrupts weather patterns and upends lives thousands of kilometres away.

stories.title: Le Cameroun auditionné par le comité des droits de l'homme des Nations unies
stories.summary: Le Cameroun auditionné par le comité des droits de l'homme des Nations unies Le Cameroun de nouveau interpellé sur sa situation en rapport aux droits de l'homme, dans le cadre d'une audition ce jeudi 22 octobre à Genève devant le comité des Nations unies chargé du suivi du pacte international relatif aux droits civils et politiques. Les préoccupations de ce comité ont porté entre autres sur l'efficacité de la lutte contre la corruption, les violences dans les régions anglophones et l'Extrême-Nord, les détentions arbitraires, les procès de civils devant les juridictions militaires, l'affaire Martinez Zogo ou encore la situation des droits des personnes homosexuelles. Publié le : 23/10/2026 - 04:30 2 min Temps de lecture Le ministre des Affaires étrangères du Cameroun, Lejeune Mbella Mbella, prend la parole lors de la 80e session de l'Assemblée générale des Nations unies, le 25 septembre 2025, au siège de l'ONU. (Image d'illustration) © AP - Pamela Smith Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite La délégation du Cameroun , conduite par son ambassadeur, le représentant permanent auprès des Nations unies, a d'abord souligné que le pays dispose d'une solide armature juridique pour la protection des droits de l'homme. « Les textes existent », a-t-elle indiqué avant d'émettre un petit bémol sur de possibles inadéquations « entre ce qui est écrit et ce qui est fait ». Sur la question précise des juridictions militaires devant lesquelles sont poursuivis des civils, la délégation a défendu le caractère légal de ces tribunaux et a ajouté que les civils y sont jugés quand les faits impliquent la participation présumée des éléments des forces de défense et de sécurité, comme dans le cas précis de l'affaire Martinez Zogo ou l'usage des armes à feu. La question sur les discriminations des personnes homosexuelles et de toutes les catégories de genre est également revenue avec insistance.

It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.” The minister of health in Guinea-Bissau, Quinhin Nantote, previously denied that the project would move forward. “This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese last week. stories.title: Paul Barril, le « barbouze » français au cœur du génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda
stories.summary: L’ancien du Groupement d’intervention de la gendarmerie nationale français est décédé ce 20 octobre. Reconverti dans le privé en Afrique, il était surtout tristement célèbre sur le continent pour son implication au côté du régime génocidaire rwandais.

stories.title: Why has a crumbling bottle plant been rebuilt in Paris? The stunning show suggesting the future is Ghana-shaped
stories.summary: Not left to rot … parts of an old bottle factory appearing in Ibrahim Mahama: The Harvest Season, Fondation Cartier, Paris. Photograph: Benoit Fougeirol View image in fullscreen Not left to rot … parts of an old bottle factory appearing in Ibrahim Mahama: The Harvest Season, Fondation Cartier, Paris. Photograph: Benoit Fougeirol Review Why has a crumbling bottle plant been rebuilt in Paris? The stunning show suggesting the future is Ghana-shaped Fondation Cartier, Paris Ibrahim Mahama put an entire factory in this exhibition exploring Ghana before and after it was ripped to shreds by colonialism. And it’s just one dazzling installation in a show full of hope Ibrahim Mahama has dug through the ruins of post-colonial Ghana, sorted through the ashes of its ancient history, picked through the industrial detritus, the corporate waste, the piles of rubbish, and found something pretty unique: hope.

stories.title: Avec Somagec, Roger Sahyoun s’impose comme le visage atypique du BTP marocain
stories.summary: Avec Somagec, Roger Sahyoun s’impose comme le visage atypique du BTP marocain Sous la direction de l’ingénieur de 74 ans, Somagec est devenu un géant marocain diversifié dont les activités s’étendent de l’Afrique subsaharienne à l’Amérique du Sud. Pour se développer, il compte sur le marché financier et non sur les banques. Le patron de Somagec vient d’achever une tournée africaine qui l’a mené de l’Angola à la Guinée équatoriale en passant par le Ghana, la RDC ou encore l’Éthiopie. © Eric Larrayadieu pour JA Par Bilal Mousjid Publié aujourd'hui à 12h29 Lecture : 6 minutes. Fichier généré le Lire dans l’app Se distinguant par son franc-parler dans un microcosme économique au ton lisse, Roger Sahyoun a pourtant la parole rare. Tant et si bien que ses sorties médiatiques de ces vingt dernières années se comptent sur les doigts d’une main.

stories.title: Au Maroc, le gouvernement El Mansouri marque déjà sa différence avec l’ère Akhannouch
stories.summary: Au Maroc, le gouvernement El Mansouri marque déjà sa différence avec l’ère Akhannouch À première vue, le programme de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri s’inscrit dans le prolongement des grands chantiers engagés par Aziz Akhannouch. Mais une lecture croisée des deux déclarations gouvernementales révèle de vrais changements de cap, certains plaçant la nouvelle majorité face à ses propres contradictions. La nouvelle cheffe du gouvernement marocain, Fatima-Ezzahra El Mansouri, a présenté son programme pour la période 2026-2031 devant les deux chambres du Parlement à Rabat, le 19 octobre 2026. © ABDEL MAJID BZIOUAT/AFP Par Jassim Ahdani Publié hier à 12h09, modifié aujourd'hui à 12h17 Lecture : 4 minutes. En 2021, Aziz Akhannouch promettait l’État social, l’emploi et la bonne gouvernance.

stories.title: Africa: Ebola - Africa CDC Convenes African Ministers of Health As Ebola Outbreak Spreads Across Three Regions
stories.summary: Ebola - Africa CDC Convenes African Ministers of Health As Ebola Outbreak Spreads Across Three Regions 21 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 21 October 2026 The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) will convene a high-level virtual meeting of African Ministers of Health on Wednesday, 28 October 2026, as the ongoing Ebola outbreak poses an escalating threat to health security across the continent. Five months into the response, the outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus continues in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with cases now reported in Kenya and Nigeria. The geographic spread across Central, Eastern and Western Africa demands urgent, coordinated action. Since Africa CDC declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May 2026, Member States, frontline health workers and partners have made sustained efforts to contain transmission. The evolving situation now calls for renewed political commitment, intensified response measures and stronger continental solidarity.

stories.summary: Le nombre de personnes séropositives a plus que doublé en l’espace de deux ans sur la Grande Ile. Une augmentation d’autant plus inquiétante que le nombre d’individus infectés est sous-évalué, car le dépistage est encore lacunaire dans le pays.

stories.title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
stories.summary: Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, Nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola By Basillioh Rukanga Reporting from Nairobi Published 21 October 2026 Kenya is grappling with its first ever outbreak of Ebola, a disease which neighbouring countries, such as Uganda and Democratic Republic of Congo, are used to dealing with. Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago. Four relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have now tested positive, meaning they are all linked to him. But concerns are rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government has sought to assure citizens. The US has warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert.

stories.title: « Le sentimentalisme, c’est fini » : au Burkina Faso, Ibrahim Traoré rétablit la peine de mort
stories.summary: Huit ans après son abolition, la peine de mort a été réintroduite ce mardi dans le code pénal burkinabè. Un virage sécuritaire assumé par la junte au pouvoir, qui y voit un moyen de lutter contre le terrorisme et l’espionnage.

stories.title: Gambia to pay victims of Yahya Jammeh's rule from proceeds of his seized US mansion
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Jammeh, who is now living in exile in Equatorial Guinea, ruled The Gambia for more than 20 years By Basillioh Rukanga Published 21 October 2026 The Gambia will use funds received from the US from the forfeiture of long-time ruler Yahya Jammeh's property to pay victims of his rule, authorities have said. The Gambia's Reparations Commission said it received $2.5m (Â£1.86m) from the sale of a mansion in Maryland owned by former leader of the West African nation. The US had in 2022 secured the right to sell the property on grounds that it was acquired through "criminal proceeds and misappropriated Gambian public funds". Jammeh ruled The Gambia for more than 20 years after taking over in a coup in 1994 - a time marked by allegations of human rights abuses forced disappearances and extrajudicial killings. How US mansion of Gambia's ex-president was seized Published 27 May 2022 Profile: Former Gambian President Yahya Jammeh Published 22 January 2017 On Tuesday, the Gambia Reparations Commission said it was "pleased to inform victims, survivors and the public that it has received a total of $2,573,414.10" from the sale of Jammeh's property.

stories.title: Paul Barril, ancien gendarme de l’Elysée devenu sulfureux mercenaire, est mort
stories.summary: Ancien numéro un du GIGN, il avait par ailleurs assuré la sécurité privée de plusieurs chefs d’Etat africains. Au cœur de la « Françafrique », il joua un rôle complexe pendant le génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda. Il s’est éteint à l’âge de 80 ans, a-t-on appris mercredi.

stories.title: ‘This petrol station is my home now’: Malawi’s fuel crisis forces desperate drivers to queue for days
stories.summary: Vehicles pack tightly into the forecourt of Meru petrol station in Zomba. Photograph: Kenneth Zindondo View image in fullscreen Vehicles pack tightly into the forecourt of Meru petrol station in Zomba. Photograph: Kenneth Zindondo ‘This petrol station is my home now’: Malawi’s fuel crisis forces desperate drivers to queue for days Shortages caused by the country’s lack of hard currency have escalated into a national emergency, with drivers waiting for a fuel tanker that may never arrive F rom the driver’s seat of his rusted minibus, Sido Sombeja stares out at a stationary sea of rear lights stretching for almost a mile down the road. It is 3am in Zomba, the old capital of Malawi , and cold night air comes through the cracked windscreen. For eight consecutive days and nights, the 40-year-old father of four has lived out of this vehicle, waiting for a fuel tanker that may never arrive.

stories.title: La guerre entre l’Etat islamique et Al-Qaida prend de l’ampleur au Sahel
stories.summary: Dans le conflit territorial et idéologique qui oppose les deux organisations djihadistes sahéliennes depuis 2019 dans cette zone frontalière, à cheval sur le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Niger, l’épisode sanglant du 9 octobre pourrait être le plus meurtrier.

stories.title: Drone strike kills more than 150 at market in Sudanese war
stories.summary: Bustling market in flames after drone strike hits disputed Sudan-South Sudan border – video Drone strike kills more than 150 at market in Sudanese war Strike pushes the toll from attacks in recent days to more than 250, underscoring lethality of Sudan’s war that ⁠erupted in April 2023 A drone strike on a market in a border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan killed at least 153 people on Monday, according to a local official, the latest in a wave of deadly attacks. The strike pushed the toll from attacks in recent days to more than 250, underscoring the lethality of airstrikes in Sudan’s war, which ⁠erupted in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces ⁠and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Yohanna Akol Ngor, the Abyei administration’s caretaker information minister, blamed Sudan’s military, without providing evidence, for Monday’s attack on Amiet market, north of Abyei town. Deaths, disappearances and forced recruitment: refugees recount horrors of relentless war in Sudan Read more “We have recorded 153 deaths,” Akol said. Sudan’s military did not respond to a request for comment.

stories.summary: Publicité Un premier cas de virus Ebola enregistré au Nigeria, dans la capitale Abuja Afrique Une femme arrivée au Nigeria par avion en provenance de l'Ouganda est porteuse du virus Ebola, a annoncé mardi le gouvernement nigérian, qui recense par ailleurs 44 cas contacts étroits. L’épidémie, déclarée en mai en République démocratique du Congo où elle a dépassé les 9 000 cas pour 4 381 décès, s’étend à plusieurs pays africains. Publié le : 20/10/2026 - 23:50 4 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 L'Assemblée nationale du Nigeria, à Abuja, le 2 novembre 2023. © Chinedu Asadu, AP Le gouvernement du Nigeria a annoncé, mardi 20 octobre, le premier cas d' Ebola sur son territoire, à Abuja, la capitale du pays le plus peuplé d'Afrique, tandis que de l'autre côté du continent, le Kenya vient de déclarer son neuvième cas. "La patiente, une femme récemment arrivée au Nigeria à bord d’un vol international en provenance d’Ouganda, a été admise dans un hôpital privé" d'Abuja "où elle a été prise en charge pendant plusieurs jours avant que le diagnostic ne soit confirmé", a déclaré dans un communiqué Muhammad Ali Pate, le ministre nigérian de la Santé. Le gouvernement a appelé "tous les établissements de santé publics et privés du pays à se mettre en état d’alerte maximale". La République démocratique du Congo est en proie depuis le mois de mai à la 17 e épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola de son histoire, devenue en quelques mois la plus meurtrière jamais connue dans ce vaste pays d' Afrique centrale.

stories.title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau
stories.summary: Robert F Kennedy Jr in Washington DC. Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA View image in fullscreen Robert F Kennedy Jr in Washington DC. Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials said on Facebook. The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m. The police search took place on Monday, involving “investigative procedures aimed at clarifying the circumstances related to the said batch of vaccines”, according to the social media post, which was translated from Portuguese.

stories.title: 'Tinubu Must Go!': Nigeria's northern protests test limits of political dissent
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5OTCD Police said the men were found in possession of 'dried leaves,' a pair of scissors and T-shirts bearing the phrase 'Tinubu Must Go!' Image: Borno State Police Command Advertisement T-shirts bearing the slogan "Tinubu Must Go!" — a reference to Nigerian President Bola Tinubu — are at the center of an escalating crackdown on dissent in Nigeria 's vast north. In September, police in the northeastern state of Borno arrested five men, aged between 21 and 44, over the shirts. Authorities have alleged the group had conspired to produce and wear them with the intention of breaching public peace. The men were subsequently charged with criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance, disturbance of public peace and thuggery. Drawing criticism from human rights groups and activists, police later explained that the arrests followed a routine patrol and that officers had found substances believed to be illicit drugs and other items on the men, arguing that they were not being prosecuted for expressing their political views.

stories.title: Madagascar, nouvelle terre de recrutement et d’influence pour la Russie
stories.summary: « Madagascar, un an après le coup d’Etat » (4/4). stories.title: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Paul Mackenzie said education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil" By Basma El Atti Reporting from Nairobi Published 20 October 2026 The eldest son of Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie, convicted of murdering 191 people, says his younger siblings were still being forced to fast as recently as two weeks ago. Dan Mackenzie, 27, said he reported the case to police, who rescued eight children, including his five younger siblings from their grandmother's house, and took them to a rescue centre. "They were basically forcibly fasted because they were denying food to them for almost three days," he tells BBC's Newsday. His father was found guilty on Monday of murdering 190 children and one adult who starved to death in Shakahola forest, near the Kenyan coast. He had ordered members of his doomsday cult to starve themselves and their children to death so they could "meet Jesus". Twenty-eight other cult leaders were also convicted of murder.

stories.title: Fleeing the frontline: Yemeni families cross Red Sea to Djibouti as Houthi conflict rages
stories.summary: Madinah Abdullah (in pink) and her family members at the Markazi humanitarian site in Obock, Djibouti, on 6 October. Photograph: Carlos Mureithi/The Guardian Their overland routes to safety blocked off, several thousand people have boarded boats to escape gunfire, bombing and a dire humanitarian situation By Carlos Mureithi in Obock A bubaker Saeed was fishing in the Red Sea off Yemen’s coast last month when he noticed explosions in the distance. His mind turned immediately to his wife and two children, and he raced back to his home village of al-Wahijah. Aircraft from the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemeni government forces had launched airstrikes in surrounding areas, targeting members of the Iran-aligned Houthi militia as its fighters approached the nearby port city of Mocha. “They were bombing Houthis while Houthis were 1km away from us,” the 50-year-old recalled. By the time he reached the shore, the rebels had arrived and were battling government forces on the ground.

stories.title: Africa: MDB Heads Strengthen Joint Action in Manila to Deliver More Financing and Greater Impact
stories.summary: MDB Heads Strengthen Joint Action in Manila to Deliver More Financing and Greater Impact 17 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner African Development Bank (Abidjan) The Heads of Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) Group met at the Asian Development Bank (ADB) headquarters in Manila today to discuss how to deliver more financing and greater impact to support developing members as they face mounting challenges. It was the Group's first-ever meeting in the Philippines, hosted by ADB as its 2026 Chair. "Conflict, economic uncertainty, high debt, inflation and disasters are placing growing pressure on our members and making development harder," said ADB President Masato Kanda, host and current Chair of the MDB Heads Group . "Our meeting in Manila was an opportunity to turn shared commitments into practical action, so we can help members protect their development gains, attract investment, and build more resilient economies." Against a backdrop of disasters, conflicts, difficult macroeconomic conditions, and constrained fiscal space, the Heads reaffirmed MDBs' readiness to provide timely financial and analytical support to protect vulnerable populations and sustain investment in jobs and resilient long-term growth. In a joint statement, the Heads welcomed the significant progress achieved this year working as a system to mobilize private capital, and on joint actions to advance jobs, nature, climate, water, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and other common development priorities, and on efforts to enhance system efficiency for greater impact at scale, in line with each institution's mandate, strategy and operational model. The role of Chair of the Heads of MDBs Group will be passed in December from ADB to the European Investment Bank Group. The Heads of MDBs Group includes the African Development Bank Group, Asian Development Bank, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Council of Europe Development Bank, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, European Investment Bank Group, Inter-American Development Bank Group, Islamic Development Bank, New Development Bank, and the World Bank Group.

Le bilan, rapporté lundi par plusieurs sources sécuritaires, locales et associatives à l’AFP, dépasse les 40 morts et s’accompagne de déplacements de population. Publié le : 20/10/2026 - 02:39 Modifié le : 20/10/2026 - 08:22 4 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Un camion-citerne incendié est abandonné au milieu de la route menant à Sikasso, la deuxième plus grande ville du Mali, le 26 mai 2026. © AFP Plus d'une quarantaine de civils ont été tués dimanche 18 octobre lors d'attaques perpétrées par des hommes armés dans la région de Ménaka, dans le nord-est du Mali , provoquant des déplacements de population, ont rapporté lundi 19 octobre à l'AFP plusieurs sources sécuritaires, locales et associatives. stories.title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister By Basma El Atti Published 20 October 2026 The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister. Mustafa Ramid, a former justice minister in an Islamist-led government, cited the saying earlier this month, in a lengthy Facebook post questioning whether a woman should hold the country's highest political office. He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men. Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy. Yet executive power remains in the hands of the 63-year-old monarch.

stories.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult

stories.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5OL1o Gaob David Timotheus Frederick (left) and Mutjinde Katjiua visited Germany this week to demand recognition and restitution Image: Christian Ditsch/epd Advertisement Gaob Daniel Timotheus Frederick was sitting in the front row of the visitors' gallery in the Bundestag this week. Wearing a suit and hat, he had traveled all the way from Namibia to see this parliamentary debate unfold. For almost 120 years, his family had been waiting for the return of human remains of their ancestor, Cornelius Frederick (sometimes spelled Fredericks), who had led the Nama resistance against German colonial rule and died on Shark Island in Germany's first concentration camp . In the name of his great-grandfather and as a member of the Nama Traditional Leaders Association (NTLA), Frederick was there to demand an "unconditioned apology" from Germany. Sitting next to him, in uniform and white gloves, with a carved lion on the handle of his walking stick, was the head of the Ovaherero Traditional Authority, Paramount Chief Mutjinde Katjiua.
